newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean, Britain to sign revised tax treaty.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean, Britain to sign revised tax treaty.

text.p: South Korea and Britain will sign a revised treaty to avoid double taxation on Friday, the foreign ministry said on Thursday.
The revision calls for a lowering of taxes on dividend, interest and surcharge income, the ministry said in a statement.
"Signing the treaty will promote bilateral trade and investment," the ministry said.
The revised treaty also adds fishery and agricultural income to the list of duties to be covered under the accord, it said.
The treaty was expected to serve as a basis for tax negotiations with other advanced nations, the statement added.
The original tax treaty was signed in 1977. The revision will be signed by British Ambassador Thomas Harris and Deputy Foreign Minister Lee Ki-choo.
The value of South Korean investment in Britain was estimated at $240 million at the end of 1995, comprising 50 projects.
British investment in South Korea is valued at $451 million (100 projects) at the end of 1995.
Over 30 Korean firms have manufacturing bases in Britain.
In July, the LG Group said LG Electronics and LG Semicon will spend $2.6 billion on semiconductor and consumer electronics facilities in Wales.
This month, Hyundai Electronics, a unit of the Hyundai Group announced that it would build a $1.5 billion semiconductor plant in Scotland.
Britain is South Korea's ninth largest trading partner.
Two-way trade between the two partners rose to $4.81 billion in the first 11 months of this year from $3.45 billion for all of 1995.
South Korea enjoyed a trade surplus of $460 million with Britain during the 11-month period, the statement said.
